summary: George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He founded and led Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870). He later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford from 1883.

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Lutheran Theological Seminary, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He taught at Yale (1927–1928) and was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Chicago (1951–1967).

George Watt worked in botany and Indology, studying at Aberdeen, King's College London, and the University of Glasgow. He was Professor of Botany at the University of Calcutta (1873) and Presidency University, later lecturing at the University of Edinburgh (~1907–1921).

George Weston Briggs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Northwestern University. He held posts at Lucknow Christian College, the University of the Pacific, and Goucher College, before serving as Professor of History of Religions at Drew University (1929–1944).

George William Brown specialized in Indology and religious studies, earning degrees from Hiram College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Christian Bible College, the College of Missions, and Lexington Theological Seminary (1927–1932).

George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in London, Paris, and Harvard, he directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute and later led a department at the Soviet Institute of Oriental Studies (~1957–1960).

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Virginia and Leiden University. He held the Chair for Descriptive Linguistics at Leiden (1996–2009) and the Chair of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed traditional monastic studies, obtained a Geshe degree at Ganden Shartse, and earned his doctorate at the University of Virginia before becoming a professor at Williams College.

Georges Cuendet was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Basel, and Paris under Charles Bally and Antoine Meillet. He taught at Gymnase de Nyon, the University of Geneva as Privatdozent of Indology (1938–1963), and the University of Lausanne.

Georges Dandoy worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Namur, Stonyhurst, Oxford, and St. Mary's College, Kurseong. He held appointments at St. Xavier's College in Mumbai, St. Mary's College, and the University of Calcutta.

Georges Dumézil was a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and Indology, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. His career included posts at Istanbul University, Uppsala, the EPHE, and the Collège de France (1949–1968).
Georges Guieysse was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Michel Bréal, Abel Bergaigne, Ferdinand de Saussure, and James Darmesteter between 1886 and 1889.

Georges Perrot was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He served as a professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris, and later directed the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1904).

Georges Redard was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. Educated at Neuchâtel, Bern, Paris under Émile Benveniste, and Tehran, he held professorships at the University of Bern from 1954 and visited at Lausanne and Collège de France.

Georges Strehly was an Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE under Paul Regnaud and Abel Bergaigne. He taught at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1879–1886) and Lycée Louis-le-Grand (1886–1906).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry. He was a professor at Blaise Pascal University (~1985–1996) and became a professor at the EPHE in 1999.

Georgij Aleksandrovič Zograf was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Vasily Beskrovny. He spent his career at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Georgij Saridanovič Ahvlediani was a linguist who studied at Kharkiv and Saint Petersburg under Friedrich Knauer, Carl Salemann, and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He was a professor at Tbilisi State University and directed the Georgian Institute of Linguistics (1949–1950).

Georgios Kozakis Typaldos was an Indologist who studied medicine at the University of Padua. He served as the Librarian at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens from approximately 1837 to 1863.

Georgios Nikolaou Hatzidakis was a linguist who studied in Athens, Leipzig, Jena, and Berlin under Brugmann, Delbrück, and others. He served as Rector of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki in 1926 and President of the Academy of Athens in 1927.
